# Power steering pump replacement

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove the second battery, loosen the pulley nut and slacken the belt to transfer it for power steering pump replacement. [t1139]

[Partial] Swap out the power steering pump and replace the associated high-pressure lines. [t2289]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the second battery if a dual setup is installed.
2. Loosen the nut on the pulley before slackening the belt to allow transfer of the pulley over.

_Procedure reported by [t1139]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t2289] [Partial]</summary>

1. Swap out the power steering pump.
2. Replace the associated high-pressure lines.

</details>

## Tools

- [Partial] Wrenches [t1139]

## Parts

- [Partial] High Pressure Line: Often the most expensive part of the swap. [t2289]
- [Partial] Power steering pump: OE or Napa reman; OEM or aftermarket [t1139, t2289]
- Seal kit: Approx $14, handles leaks but not impeller issues [t1139]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a 2-inch body lift to gain clearance if available. [t1139]
- Transfer the pulley over after loosening its nut before fully slacking the belt. [t1139]
- The pump can be loud if air bubbles get into it from a leaky return line. [t2289]
- Used pumps are available cheaply via eBay. [t2289]
